output:
**What I found**
The boundary gate does not work. It has stayed green because it checks nothing, not because the code is clean. In `eslint.config.mjs`, the two blocks both configure `no-restricted-syntax`. ESLint flat config replaces a rule's options with the last matching block instead of merging them. So the `**/*.js` block (lines 15–26), which only forbids `debugger`, overwrites the auth-internals selector (lines 6–12) for every file under `src/`. `src/billing/invoice.js:1` gets through because the rule that should catch it is never applied. The fix is to bring back the scope the gate claims and add a check that proves it fires (the record calls this RESTORE).

**Why it matters**
Every past green run said nothing about auth boundaries. Other files may already break the same rule. Once restored, the gate will fail on `invoice.js` right away. `src/auth/index.js` exports only `issueSession`, not `signToken`, so billing has no public way to sign a token yet. If nothing changes, any module can keep reaching into auth internals while CI stays green.

**Do this first**
1. Move the boundary to its own rule key so the two blocks no longer clash. In `eslint.config.mjs`, replace the first block's `no-restricted-syntax` with:
   ```js
   'no-restricted-imports': ['error', { patterns: [{
       group: ['**/auth/internal/**'],
       message: 'Import auth through src/auth/index.js, never its internals.',
   }]}],
   ```
   Then add a negative control to CI that runs the code through the assembled config and expects the declared message and exit code 1:
   ```sh
   echo "import { signToken } from '../auth/internal/token.js';" \
     | npx eslint --stdin --stdin-filename src/billing/__control__.js \
     | grep -q "never its internals"
   ```
   Without this control, a later block can silently shadow the rule again.
2. In the same change, fix `invoice.js`. Either auth publishes a public invoice-token function in `src/auth/index.js` and billing calls it, or the import stays behind one named, owned `eslint-disable-next-line` that points to the tracking issue. Whether auth should expose token signing to billing is an API decision for the auth owner (`architecture-guidelines`).
3. After restoring, run `npm run lint` and make every new violation either fixed or named. Don't add a blanket baseline.

**What I did not check**
- I couldn't run commands in this session, so the shadowing comes from reading the config against flat-config merge rules, not from a run. `npx eslint --print-config src/billing/invoice.js` confirms it: the resolved `no-restricted-syntax` will list only the `DebuggerStatement` selector.
- I didn't check whether other files break the restored rule. `npm run lint` after step 1 shows that.
- I didn't look at CI history to confirm the gate has never been red. Without that record it counts as unproven anyway.

```text
Gate:         eslint no-restricted-syntax auth-internals boundary (eslint.config.mjs:1-14), via `npm run lint`, merge-blocking on PRs
Stage:        PR/CI static analysis (lint)
Trigger:      narrowed — passed while a known-bad input existed (src/billing/invoice.js:1)
Proof:        UNPROVEN — no negative control; no recorded red run
Scope:        declared src/**/*.js minus src/auth/** / effective none (options shadowed by **/*.js block, eslint.config.mjs:15-26) / delta all auth-internal imports outside src/auth unchecked
Baseline:     none
Status:       BLOCKING (nominally; boundary rule inert)
Decision:     RESTORE
Guard:        CI negative control: stdin import of ../auth/internal/token.js as src/billing/__control__.js must exit 1 with "never its internals"
Handoff:      architecture-guidelines — auth public API for invoice token signing (src/auth/index.js exports no signer)
Next action:  Move boundary to no-restricted-imports, add the stdin control to CI, resolve invoice.js:1 in the same change
Verification: Not run — no shell in this session; confirm with `npx eslint --print-config src/billing/invoice.js`, then the control command, then `npm run lint`
```
